seoTitle: Flaccy — Lossless FLAC Player for iPhone, Apple Watch and Mac
metaDescription: Play the music you own at full quality, with a real equalizer. Flaccy handles FLAC, ALAC, WAV, AIFF, MP3 and AAC with gapless playback, synced lyrics, Last.fm scrobbling and a standalone Apple Watch app. No account, no ads, nothing uploaded. Free to try.
heroHeadline: Play the music you own, at full quality
heroSubhead: Flaccy plays your FLAC, ALAC, WAV, AIFF, MP3 and AAC files exactly as they were mastered — gapless, with a real equalizer, synced lyrics, Last.fm scrobbling and an Apple Watch app that works without your phone. No account, no ads, and your files never leave your device.
highlights: Codec, bit depth and sample rate on every track, from CD quality to Hi-Res
A real equalizer: drag the curve, import AutoEq profiles, give every output its own setting
Gapless playback, synced lyrics and every play scrobbled to Last.fm, even offline
A standalone Apple Watch app, a native Mac app and a free Linux app

features.title: See exactly what you're hearing
features.body: Every album and track wears its codec, bit depth and sample rate, from AAC 16/44.1 to FLAC 24/96, and a Lossless filter shows what is worth a good pair of headphones.

features.title: A real equalizer
features.body: Drag the curve and hear it change, or switch to Advanced for up to ten bands with bells, shelves, filters and adjustable Q. Sixteen presets, your own saved profiles, and import of Equalizer APO and AutoEq text to tune for your headphones. Every output remembers its own setting, so AirPods, a wired DAC and the speaker each sound right. Automatic headroom keeps boosts from clipping, Hold to compare is level-matched so louder never wins, and gapless playback stays intact. On iPhone, Mac and Linux.

features.title: Your library, organized
features.body: Bring music in from the Files app, a USB drive, a NAS or any folder, and Flaccy keeps your folder structure. Messy filenames and scene releases are cleaned up automatically with AI cleanup (included in the trial and in Lifetime), duplicate songs are listed once, and you can swap any cover for your own.

features.title: Gapless, as albums were made
features.body: Albums flow track to track with zero silence — exact for FLAC, ALAC, WAV and AIFF. The queue survives relaunches, so the music picks up where you left it.

features.title: Lyrics that follow every word
features.body: Synced lyrics with tap-to-seek, from your own .lrc files or looked up automatically. Plus AirPlay, a sleep timer, Lock Screen and Dynamic Island controls, and a Now Playing screen worth looking at, in light or dark.

features.title: Scrobble everything
features.body: Sign in with Last.fm and every play is scrobbled, even offline, with automatic retry. Listening charts, artist bios, a wantlist for the records you're hunting and smart playlists made from your own listening.

features.title: Year in Music
features.body: Your listening year as shareable story cards and a poster: top artists, albums and the numbers behind them, rendered from your own plays.

features.title: Phone-free on Apple Watch
features.body: Sync albums to your wrist and play them offline: gapless, shuffle, repeat and AirPods controls, with storage-smart sync that knows what fits. No iPhone in your pocket.

features.title: Honest about audio
features.body: The built-in Listening Guide explains what actually reaches your ears: Bluetooth codecs, why lossless can't reach AirPods, and when FLAC is worth it. No snake oil.

features.title: Private by design
features.body: No account, no ads and nothing uploaded: your files stay on your device. AI cleanup, when you use it, sends file names and tags, never audio, and Last.fm is entirely optional.

features.title: Made for iPhone Duo
features.body: On the inner display the library sits beside Now Playing, lyrics and artwork take their own panes, and every screen ends at the fold. On the outer display it is a regular, fast iPhone player.

features.title: Flaccy for Mac
features.body: A native Liquid Glass Mac app that wears the colour of your music, with the equalizer in its own window beside your library (⌥⌘E). Watch a folder and new files appear instantly, control playback from the menu bar player and your media keys, sort a multi-column song list, browse keyboard-first and export full-resolution Year in Music posters. Available on the Mac App Store.

features.title: Flaccy for Linux
features.body: A native GTK4 app that tints itself with the colour of whatever is playing, with gapless GStreamer playback, MPRIS media keys, Last.fm scrobbling, synced lyrics, listening stats and the same equalizer, in light or dark. Free and open source. Install with one command — curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guitaripod/flaccy/master/linux/get-flaccy.sh | sh — or from the AUR with yay -S flaccy-bin.

howItWorks.body: Pick files or whole folders in the Files app, copy over USB, or connect a NAS. Flaccy shows what it is doing while it indexes, then opens straight into your library. Try it right away with the free sample album.
Browse albums, artists, songs and playlists, then play gaplessly with synced lyrics, AirPlay and full controls on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island.
Sign in with Last.fm once and every play is counted, even offline. Watch your charts grow and unwrap your Year in Music.

faq.q: What audio formats does Flaccy play?
faq.a: FLAC, ALAC, WAV, AIFF, MP3, AAC, M4A and CAF. Playback is gapless for all of them, but only lossless files (FLAC, ALAC, WAV, AIFF) are sample-exact at the seams: MP3 and AAC carry encoder padding that iOS does not strip, so a lossy rip of a segued album can click where the lossless one does not. DSD is not supported.

Yes, on iPhone, Mac and Linux. Drag the curve in Simple mode, or switch to Advanced for up to ten bands with bells, shelves, high-pass and low-pass filters and adjustable Q. It ships with sixteen presets, saves your own, and imports Equalizer APO and AutoEq profile text so you can tune for your headphones. Each output (AirPods, a wired DAC, the speaker) keeps its own setting and switches when you do. Automatic headroom prevents clipping, and Hold to compare is level-matched so louder never sounds better. With the equalizer off or flat the signal passes through untouched, and gapless playback is unaffected. The Apple Watch app plays through the system and has no equalizer.

faq.q: Do I need an account or a streaming subscription?
faq.a: No. Flaccy plays files you already own. There is no account, no upload and no ads. A Last.fm account is optional, only for scrobbling. AI cleanup sends file names and tags, never audio, to identify messy albums.

Free to download, with a 7-day free trial that starts the first time you play your own music. After that, keep everything with a one-time Lifetime purchase ($12.99), or choose the yearly plan ($7.99 a year, renews until you cancel). The iPhone app (with Apple Watch) and the Mac app are separate purchases. Flaccy for Linux is free and open source.

faq.q: How do I get my music into Flaccy?
faq.a: Pick files or whole folders in the Files app, copy them over USB, or connect a NAS through Files and import from there. Folders keep their structure, so compilations and multi-disc albums stay together. Messy folder names and scene releases are identified and cleaned up automatically.

Yes. Sign in with your Last.fm account and every play is scrobbled, even offline, with automatic retry once you're back online. You also get loved tracks, listening charts and artist bios matched to your library.

faq.q: Is there an Apple Watch app?
faq.a: Yes, a true standalone player. Sync albums from your iPhone, then play them offline from your wrist with gapless playback, shuffle, repeat and AirPods controls. No iPhone required.

faq.q: Is lossless audio worth it on iPhone?
faq.a: It depends on how you listen, and Flaccy is honest about it. The built-in Listening Guide explains Bluetooth codecs, why lossless can't reach AirPods, when FLAC is genuinely worth it and what blind tests really show.

faq.q: Does it work on iPhone Duo?
faq.a: Yes. On the inner display the library sits beside Now Playing, lyrics and artwork get their own panes, and layouts end at the fold. On the outer display it behaves like a regular iPhone.

Yes. Flaccy for Mac is a native Liquid Glass app on the Mac App Store. Point it at a folder and new files appear instantly, control playback from the menu bar player and your media keys, sort a multi-column song list and export full-resolution Year in Music posters. It is a separate purchase from the iOS app.

Yes. Flaccy for Linux is a free, open source GTK4 app with gapless playback, MPRIS media keys, Last.fm scrobbling, synced lyrics and a full equalizer, with an adaptive theme that retints the whole app with the colour of whatever you're playing. Install it with the one-line command in the Flaccy for Linux section or from the AUR with yay -S flaccy-bin.
